title: Announce a live call in the parent chat: a message a human reads, plus an extension key a client acts on
description:
Route (a) of decision mimid-1wgh.114, reshaped 2026-11-23 after Mark
asked what the Right Thing was. It was first written as "send a
mimi-content-10 §5.10 session part carrying the call room's mimi:// URI".
That was wrong, and the reasons matter more than the conclusion.

WHY THE §5.10 SESSION PART IS THE WRONG FIELD.

§5.10's own prose: "Joining a conference via an EXTERNAL URL is possible.
The link could be rendered to the user, requiring a click." Its worked
example is https://example.com/join/12345. The field is about external
conference services.

And a mimi:// room URI is an identifier, not an action: protocol-07 §2.1
defines room URIs, and nothing anywhere defines "join the call in this
room" as what a client does with one. Putting one in §5.10's url would be
mimid's private extension wearing a standard field's clothes -- it would
look interoperable and be understood by nobody else.

THE GAP THAT MISTAKE WAS HIDING, and it is the real finding: nothing in
MIMI signals that a call is LIVE. room-policy-04 §5 gives the structure
(a parent-dependent room), mimi-content-10 §5.10 gives external URLs,
draft-atwood-mimi-calls gives the keys. No draft says "a call is
happening in room X right now". Filed separately as bead
mimid-1wgh.37.111.

WHAT TO BUILD INSTEAD, Mark's decision 2026-11-23:

1. JOINING IS A MIMI OPERATION, not a link click. The call is the room: a
   client is invited to it (which Store::start_call already does) and
   sees parent_room pointing at the chat, which is all it needs.
   ietf-wg-mimi/mimi-room-policy#45, Mark's own open PR, adds
   canJoinFromParent -- "a participant of the parent room can join a
   parent-dependent room without being added" -- which is the
   self-service version of exactly this case. Nothing to invent.

2. THE ANNOUNCEMENT GOES IN THE EXTENSIONS MAP. mimi-content-10 §4.3 and
   §8.2.1 define a per-message extensions map with an IANA registry, and
   say "Negative integer and text string keys are only for private use".
   So: an ordinary message in the PARENT chat whose text any client
   renders ("Alice started a call"), carrying a private-use extension key
   naming the call room. A client that knows the key offers Join; every
   other client shows the sentence and the user is not left wondering why
   an empty room appeared. This is the same pattern as the component id
   at 0xf021 (decision mimid-1wgh.112): a private-use value, marked
   provisional, with the draft asking IANA for a real one.

3. §5.10 KEEPS ITS REAL JOB: an external conference URL, when someone
   actually supplies one. Separate feature, bead mimid-1wgh.114.3.

FIRST THING TO DECIDE, before any code: the extension key itself.
§4.3 allows a negative integer or a text string. Recommendation: a TEXT
STRING, because two implementations picking private negative integers
will collide and two picking text strings will not, and the key is
visible on the wire where a reader benefits from it naming itself. It
is INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC either way and needs a decision bead with
the chosen spelling, the value's CBOR type (§8.2.1's registry wants a
type, and "a map containing all the related fields" is what it
encourages for related data), and what goes in it: the call room's URI
at least, and whether anything else.

WHY THIS DEMOS BETTER, which was Mark's other requirement: the chat shows
"Alice started a call", our client offers Join, media flows, and the
point lands -- both sides derived the same key from the MLS group with
nothing sent. A clickable link would weaken it, because "so what is the
link pointing at?" has no good answer.
notes:
REMOVED by Mark 2026-11-25: the announcement is gone, with crates/mimid-agent-store/src/call.rs (~390 lines), its hex fixtures, announce_call_ended, CallOptions' media and subject, and the IRC notice of bead mimid-1wgh.114.6.

WHY: Mark asked whether the call work was overengineered, and this was the clearest yes. ~390 lines of private-use CBOR carried a room URI, media kinds and a subject. The media kinds and subject could have ridden in the call room's own metadata (HostOptions::child_of already takes a name and is passed ""), so the mechanism's only irreducible job was telling clients that CANNOT join that a call happened.

WHAT IS LOST, and it is a real loss and not a cleanup:

* A client with no VTC surface learns nothing about a call. The only trace outside the call's own room is the MLS invite into it, which such a client cannot read as a call.
* No end marker, so nothing says a call stopped.
* mediaTypes and subject die at the creating client's own object: whoever joins a call they did not start knows neither, and the SDP is all that says what media it carries.
* Bead mimid-1wgh.114.6's IRC work is undone. An IRC user gets no notice that a call started elsewhere, which is the silence that bead was filed to fix.

Decisions mimid-1wgh.116, .117, .124 and .128 described this mechanism and are now historical.
close_reason: Implemented. The announcement is an ordinary message in the parent chat carrying tag:reviewcommit.com,2026:mimid:live-call per decision mimid-1wgh.128 (which superseded .116 and .124). crates/mimid-agent-store/src/call.rs holds the key, the codec and the receiving-side reader; Store::start_call_with sends it and announce_call_ended sends the advisory end; the JMAP path passes the client's media kinds and subject through. Commit c9c5e98f, tests in mimid-agent-store/tests/call_announcement.rs and tests/calls.rs. Decision mimid-1wgh.117's rules are in the module docs and docs/agent.md.
